terms.comment: The plain classical word for a way or a route; its use for a route up a climbing wall is ours. Traupman and Morgan–Owens name the climber and the sport (ascēnsor, ascēnsiō, Traupman 48; rūpium ascēnsor, M-O s.v. hike: rock climber) but have no word for the route.

sources: Lewis & Short: via
L&S ansa documents handles and things taken hold of. The hold and route senses above are our semantic extensions.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 48.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. hike: rock climber.
